newsitem.title: USA: Reno rebuffs senator on probe of campaign funding.
newsitem.headline: Reno rebuffs senator on probe of campaign funding.

text.p: The Justice Department rejected on Tuesday a Republican senator's request for an immediate independent investigation of alleged illegal contributions to President Clinton's re-election campaign.

Sen. John McCain of Arizona asked a month ago for the appointment of an independent counsel to probe whether Clinton and the Democratic Party received illegal foreign contributions during the just-completed campaign.

McCain, a key supporter of defeated Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, cited news reports that the Democrats got nearly $1 million in contributions from individuals tied to the Lippo Group, an Indonesian company.

In seeking an independent probe, McCain said it would be impossible for Clinton administration officials to determine, free of political considerations, if there had been any violations of the law or ethical lapses.

The Justice Department, in a letter approved by Attorney General Janet Reno and signed by acting Assistant Attorney General Mark Richard, denied the request for the time being but said it would remain under review.
Richard said McCain had failed to meet the law's requirement of providing "specific, credible evidence" that a person covered under the independent counsel act had committed a federal crime.
"An independent counsel cannot be appointed to explore the possibility of ethical lapses, as you suggest," Richard said in the three-page letter.

"Nor can an independent counsel assume the role of the independent regulatory agencies, such as the Federal Election Commission, to determine whether campaign financing by political organisations was in conformity with the law," he said.

Nonetheless, Richard said McCain's allegations would be carefully reviewed by a Justice Department task force examining a wide range of allegations involving campaign financing practices in the recent national election.
He said the task force would determine which allegations, if any, warranted further criminal investigation and any other action by the Justice Department or an independent counsel.

The letter was almost identical to one sent Friday rejecting a request by the citizens' lobbying group Common Cause for an independent probe of alleged violations of the finance laws by both the Democratic and Republican presidential campaigns during the 1996 primaries.

McCain and four other congressional Republicans last month sent a separate, more detailed request for an independent counsel to investigate allegations the Democrats committed federal election violations.

Among the eight incidents cited were the Democratic patry's receipt of $425,000 from an Indonesia couple with ties to the Lippo Group and Democratic National Committee official John Huang's fund-raising activities.
The Justice Department has yet to respond to that request.
